title: Keynote Speakers
text:
Professor of Biostatistics, Department of Epidemiology and Biostatistics, Imperial College London


Marta Blangiardo’s research focused on environmental exposure estimation and spatial and spatio-temporal modelling for disease mapping and risk assessment. Her work includes air pollution modelling, environmental epidemiology, and climate-change-related health impacts. She leads the Biostatistics and Data Science theme of the MRC Centre for Environment and Health and is co-author of Spatial and Spatio-Temporal Bayesian Models with R-INLA.

For more information, visit her home page

title: Keynote Speakers
text:
Haziq Jamil

Research Specialist, CEMSE Division, KAUST


Haziq Jamil’s research lies at the intersection of statistical theory, computational methods, and social science applications. He obtained his PhD and MSc in Statistics from the London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE), and his BSc from Warwick University. At KAUST, he works with Prof. Håvard Rue in the BAYESCOMP group, tackling the computational challenges of Bayesian inference for modern psychometric applications of latent variable modelling.

For more information, visit his home page

title: Programme
text:
EnviBayes Student Paper Competition

The workshop will also host a dedicated session featuring the winners of the 2027 EnviBayes Student Paper Competition. This annual competition recognises outstanding student-led research in Bayesian methodology and applications to environmental sciences. Winners receive a certificate and monetary award and are invited to present their work in the dedicated EnviBayes session.
Talks presented in the EnviBayes session will also be eligible for the Best Student/ECR Talk prize above.
Applications for the 2027 EnviBayes Student Paper Competition close on 1 December 2026 at 5pm EST. Full details on eligibility and how to apply are available on the EnviBayes Student Paper Competition page.

title: EnviBayes-INLA workshop
text: The EnviBayes–INLA Workshop 2027 is the first joint meeting between the EnviBayes and INLA workshop series, bringing together researchers developing Bayesian methods for environmental, ecological, spatial and spatio-temporal statistics. The programme will feature keynote lectures, contributed talks, poster sessions, and hands-on tutorials, covering a broad range of topics including INLA, spatial modelling, extreme value analysis, climate and weather, ecology, epidemiology, and environmental applications. The workshop builds on the success of previous EnviBayes workshops (2023, 2025) and the INLA: Past, Present and Future workshop, creating a unique opportunity for collaboration between these two vibrant research communities.

title: Tutorials
text:
The following tutorials will take place prior to the EnviBayes-INLA Workshop. Please refer to the main workshop page for tutorial fees. The fee includes one coffee break per tutorial; lunch is not included.






NoteGetting more Complex with Environmental Modelling: from mgcv to Stan




Dave Miller, Biomathematics and Statistics Scotland (BioSS) & UK Centre for Ecology and Hydrology (UKCEH)

This tutorial will provide a brief introduction to making the jump from modelling in the GAM-centric package mgcv to the more general Stan probabilistic programming language. It will give some background on how the innards of mgcv work and how we can adapt these constructions to be used in more general ecological and environmental models. Adding spatial and temporal smoothers and structured random effects can help to add generality and flexibility to our models. Using mgcv to generate these structures makes things easier, especially when it comes to highly complex effects.
Duration: 3 hours
Date: Monday 21\(^\text{st}\) June, 2027
Time: 09:00 – 12:30
Venue: Room 116, School of Mathematics & Statistics









NoteINLA AND BEYOND: Bayesian Hierarchical Modelling with inlabru




Jafet Belmont Osuna, University of Glasgow

INLA, a powerful tool for efficiently fitting complex spatial models, comes with a steep learning curve. This workshop introduces inlabru – a user-friendly interface to INLA. Learn to specify models intuitively, handle spatial data efficiently, and focus on data structures and interpretation, rather than computational complexity!
Duration: 3 hours
Date: Monday 21\(^\text{st}\) June, 2027
Time: 13:30 – 17:00
Venue: Room 116, School of Mathematics & Statistics

Expected Behaviour
All members and participants must maintain a professional, respectful, and productive environment free from discrimination, harassment, and retaliation. Debate is encouraged but must be conducted with professionalism, respect, and courtesy.
Unacceptable Behaviour
Prohibited behaviours include threats, harassment, disrespectful comments or actions targeting personal characteristics (e.g., gender, race, religion, etc.), intimidation, stalking, inappropriate physical contact, and unwelcome sexual attention. Disorderly or disruptive conduct and violations of event rules are also unacceptable.
These standards apply to all participants. Anyone who experiences, observes, or has knowledge of a violation should bring it to the attention of Daniela Castro-Camilo and Jafet Belmont.

The University of Glasgow is situated in the West End, with a variety of small hotels and guest houses nearby, as well as easy links to City Centre hotels via the Subway.
The closest Subway station to the main University campus is Hillhead. For City Centre hotels, the closest stations are Buchanan Street and St. Enoch. The journey between the West End and City Centre takes around 10 minutes by Subway.
Delegates are advised to book early to guarantee availability at their preferred hotel.

🛂 Visa Information
Delegates travelling from outside the UK should check whether they need a visa or an Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) to attend. As of February 2026, most visa-exempt visitors (including from the EU, US, Canada, and Australia) now require an ETA before travelling — this is separate from a visa and is usually approved within a few days, but we recommend applying at least 2–3 weeks before travel. Check requirements via the UK government’s visa/ETA checker.






NoteInvitation letter for visa application



If you require an official letter of invitation to support your visa or ETA application, please tick the related box in the registration form. If you forget to do this or require further assistance, please get in touch with the organising committee with your name, affiliation, and passport details as they appear on your travel documents.

🚇 Exploring & Getting Around Glasgow
Glasgow is a vibrant and compact city with plenty to offer delegates outside of conference sessions.
The city has a range of cultural attractions including the works of Charles Rennie Mackintosh and many museums and art galleries offering free entry.
If you’re extending your stay, Glasgow has excellent travel connections for exploring Scotland and an exciting selection of year-round tours leaving daily for the Scottish Highlands.
Delegates can look forward to a warm welcome in a city voted ‘world’s friendliest city’ by Rough Guides.
